_lib_gates.py calls reads.tracker_dir(repo_root) at 8 sites (search_files output) but no test asserts the propagated error type at that surface.
ABSENCE: the class of regression the change guards (SystemExit killing the MCP process) is asserted only indirectly via a static AST source scan, not by exercising the gate/MCP propagation path.
advisory.finding: The motivating behavior of the fix — that a TrackerRootError (an Exception, not a BaseException) now propagates out of the library/MCP read surface so FastMCP's `except Exception` can catch it instead of the process dying — is not verified behaviorally. Tests cover tracker_dir raising and the CLI mapping, but no test exercises the _lib_gates/_mcp_reads surface to assert it surfaces a catchable error rather than terminating the host. A regression that re-introduced a SystemExit only in the MCP call path (e.g. a wrapper re-raising as SystemExit) would not be caught by the raise tests, and the source-scan only inspects static text, not the propagation contract through the gate surface.
scenarios: A future change wraps tracker_dir in the MCP path and converts the RebarError into a SystemExit again — the raise tests still pass (tracker_dir itself still raises RebarError) and the process would still die under FastMCP.
